subject.title: [Bug] gateway shutdown timed out: node report shows active child process handle; leaves dirty shutdown + lane wait

question: Should normal SIGTERM/SIGINT gateway shutdown cancel managed active runs and their child exec processes, or preserve background/yielded exec sessions unless an explicit restart or process-kill path is used?
rationale: Current source and tests intentionally preserve active/background exec work on normal shutdown, so changing that behavior is an operator-safety and product contract decision rather than a mechanical patch.

options.title: Define bounded managed-process shutdown
options.body: On normal stop, reject new work and cancel maintainer-approved managed run/exec scopes before the watchdog, with an explicit documented exception for any background process class that should survive.

options.title: Preserve current normal-stop behavior
options.body: Keep normal shutdown from aborting active/background exec work and treat this as a diagnostics/docs/support issue instead of runtime cancellation.

options.title: Defer to session exec-control design
options.body: Keep this open until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/12554 defines the process-control contract, then reuse that contract for gateway shutdown.

recommendation.title: Define bounded managed-process shutdown
recommendation.body: On normal stop, reject new work and cancel maintainer-approved managed run/exec scopes before the watchdog, with an explicit documented exception for any background process class that should survive.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest recent gateway/process-control history and was pulled into the issue timeline.
